newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee roaster KJS raises retail prices.
newsitem.headline: German coffee roaster KJS raises retail prices.

text.p: German coffee roaster Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) announced on Friday it would raise the retail price of its roasted coffee products by two marks per kilo effective March 10.
The German market leader cited higher raw materials prices for the increase.

Roasters' buying-in prices of high quality arabicas had jumped by 45 percent since December 1996 to 150 cents per lb and the dollar had risen by 10 percent to 1.65 marks in that period, the statement said.
Stocks at origin and in consumer countries were low and reduced crop expectations in Brazil made higher green coffee prices look likely over a long period, it said.
KJS, which is a part of the Philip Morris group, said coffee consumption in the Americas and Europe was rising, which meant increased import requirements from origin.
KJS had registered a trend to increasing coffee consumption in Germany since the second half of 1996 after slight decreases in 1994 and 1995.
Annemieke Wijn, managing director of the Jacobs coffee unit within KJS, was quoted as saying cost pressures were an industry-wide phenomenon.
The unit had sales of 2.2 billion marks in 1996 and a 28.5 percent market share in Germany, the second largest coffee consuming country in the world.
KJS said is expected innovative products to contribute to a rise in coffee tonnages and sales revenue in 1997.
